bigPicture: **Limits** describe local behaviour: what f(x) approaches as x approaches a (even if f(a) is undefined).
**Continuity** means no surprises at a point: lim f(x) = f(a). Discontinuities are removable, jump or infinite.
The **derivative** is the slope of the tangent / the instantaneous rate of change; **differentiable ⇒ continuous**, not the reverse.
Memorise the **derivative table** and the **sum, product, quotient and chain rules** – used constantly in economics, finance and statistics.

concepts.name: Limits: intuitive idea and limit laws
concepts.simple: The limit is the value the function heads towards as x gets close to a – it does not matter what happens exactly at a.
exam: **lim_(x→a) f(x) = L**: f(x) gets arbitrarily close to L as x gets close to a (from either side), without necessarily f(a) = L, or even f(a) being defined.
**Limit laws** (both limits exist): lim(f + g) = lim f + lim g · lim(fg) = lim f · lim g · lim(f/g) = lim f / lim g (lim g ≠ 0).
concepts.example: f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) = x + 1 for x ≠ 1 ⇒ lim_(x→1) f(x) = 2 although f(1) is undefined.

concepts.name: One-sided limits and limits at infinity
concepts.simple: Approach from the left and from the right; the limit exists only if both sides agree. At infinity, divide by the highest power of x.
exam: - Left limit lim_(x→a⁻) f(x), right limit lim_(x→a⁺) f(x). **lim_(x→a) f(x) exists ⇔ both one-sided limits exist and coincide.**
- **Limits at infinity:** behaviour as x becomes infinitely big; **divide numerator and denominator by the highest power of x**.
- f(x) = |x| at 0: both one-sided limits 0 ⇒ limit 0.
- f(x) = 1 for x < 0, 2 for x ≥ 0: left limit 1, right limit 2 ⇒ **the limit does not exist**.

concepts.name: Continuity and types of discontinuity
concepts.simple: Continuous = you can draw the graph without lifting the pen. Holes, jumps and vertical asymptotes break continuity.
exam: **f is continuous at a if lim_(x→a) f(x) = f(a)**, i.e. (i) f(a) is defined, (ii) the limit exists, (iii) they are equal.

- Polynomials, exponentials, logarithms (on their domain) and trig functions are continuous wherever defined; sums, products, quotients and compositions of continuous functions are continuous (where defined).
| Type | Meaning |
| **Removable** (hole) | limit exists but ≠ f(a), or f(a) undefined – fixable by redefining f(a) |
| **Jump** | one-sided limits exist but differ |
| **Infinite** (asymptote) | the function grows without bound near a |
concepts.example: f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) with f(1) := 2 is continuous at 1 (the removable discontinuity is fixed).

concepts.name: Differentiability: definition and interpretation
concepts.simple: The derivative is the slope of the curve at one point: how fast f changes right there.
exam: f is **differentiable at a** if **f′(a) = lim_(h→0) [f(a + h) − f(a)]/h** exists.
f′(a) is the **slope of the tangent** at x = a and the **instantaneous rate of change** of f at a.
**Differentiable at a ⇒ continuous at a.** The converse is false: |x| is continuous but not differentiable at 0 (a corner).
concepts.example: |x| has a corner at 0: continuous, no unique tangent slope.

concepts.name: Derivatives of special functions
concepts.simple: A short table of the derivatives you must know by heart.
exam: | c (constant) | 0 |
| xⁿ | n·xⁿ⁻¹ |
| eˣ | eˣ |
| aˣ | aˣ·ln a |
| ln x | 1/x |
| sin x | cos x |
| cos x | −sin x |

concepts.name: Rules of differentiation
concepts.simple: Sum: differentiate term by term. Product: ‘first′ × second + first × second′’. Quotient: ‘(top′·bottom − top·bottom′)/bottom²’. Chain: outer′ at the inner × inner′.
exam: - (f ± g)′ = f′ ± g′ (**sum rule**) · (cf)′ = c f′ (**constant multiple**)
- **(fg)′ = f′g + fg′** (product rule)
- **(f/g)′ = (f′g − fg′)/g²** (g ≠ 0) (quotient rule)
- **(g ∘ f)′(x) = g′(f(x))·f′(x)** (chain rule)

concepts.name: Higher-order derivatives
concepts.simple: Differentiate again and again: f″ is the derivative of f′.
concepts.exam: The derivative of f′ is the **second derivative f″** (or f⁽²⁾); repeat for f‴, f⁽⁴⁾, …, f⁽ⁿ⁾. Higher derivatives are used to analyse convexity and extrema (Session 6).
concepts.example: f(x) = x⁴ − 3x²: f′ = 4x³ − 6x, f″ = 12x² − 6, f‴ = 24x. For ln x: f′ = 1/x, f″ = −1/x².

connections: **Session 4:** the derivative table covers the special functions.
**Session 6:** f′ gives monotonicity and critical points, f″ gives convexity.
**Math A Lecture 1:** the limit of a **sequence** (ε-definition) is the discrete version of a limit.

questions: Compute limits by cancelling factors or dividing by the highest power.
Check continuity at a point (three conditions) and classify discontinuities.
Differentiate with product, quotient and chain rules; compute f″.
traps: The limit at a does not depend on f(a).
Quotient rule: f′g **minus** fg′ – order matters.
mistakes: Forgetting the inner derivative in the chain rule (ln(x² + 1) → 2x/(x² + 1)).
Saying a limit exists when the one-sided limits differ.

memorize: **Table:** c→0, xⁿ→nxⁿ⁻¹, eˣ→eˣ, aˣ→aˣ ln a, ln x→1/x, sin→cos, cos→−sin.

practice.question: f(x) = 1 for x < 0, 2 for x ≥ 0. lim_(x→0) f(x)…
Which is NOT a condition for continuity at a?

questions.question: f(x) = (x² − 1)/(x − 1) with f(1) = 2 is at x = 1…
Which implication is correct?
questions.explanation: |x| is the counterexample to the converse.

questions.question:
Differentiate:
(a) f(x) = x³ sin x
(b) g(x) = eˣ/(x² + 1) (simplify)
(c) h(x) = (2x + 1)eˣ + ln(x² + 1)
questions.model:
(a) f′(x) = 3x² sin x + x³ cos x (product rule).
(b) g′(x) = [eˣ(x² + 1) − eˣ·2x]/(x² + 1)² = eˣ(x − 1)²/(x² + 1)² (quotient rule).
(c) h′(x) = 2eˣ + (2x + 1)eˣ + 2x/(x² + 1) = (2x + 3)eˣ + 2x/(x² + 1).

questions.question: State the definition of continuity at a point and name and explain the three types of discontinuity from the slides.
questions.model: f is continuous at a if lim_(x→a) f(x) = f(a): f(a) defined, limit exists, both equal. Removable (hole): limit exists but ≠ f(a) or f(a) undefined – fixable by redefining f(a). Jump: one-sided limits exist but differ. Infinite (asymptote): f grows without bound near a.
